CHANGE TICKET:
Make PRN the only router injecting customer 3's route.

UNIFIED DIFF:
--- a/configs/CPK.cfg
+++ b/configs/CPK.cfg
@@ -59,4 +59,8 @@
 ip prefix-list PL_CUST3 seq 5 permit 172.16.3.0/24
 !
+ip prefix-list PL_NO_C3 seq 5 permit 172.16.3.0/24
+!
+route-map RM_BGP2OSPF deny 5
+ match ip address prefix-list PL_NO_C3
 route-map RM_BGP2OSPF permit 10
  match ip address prefix-list PL_ALL_CUST
--- a/configs/PRN.cfg
+++ b/configs/PRN.cfg
@@ -59,4 +59,8 @@
 ip prefix-list PL_CUST3 seq 5 permit 172.16.3.0/24
 !
+ip prefix-list PL_NO_C3 seq 5 permit 172.16.0.0/16 le 24
+!
+route-map RM_BGP2OSPF deny 5
+ match ip address prefix-list PL_NO_C3
 route-map RM_BGP2OSPF permit 10
  match ip address prefix-list PL_ALL_CUST


Hosts: c1-host(172.16.1.10,cust1,mtu 1500), c2-host(172.16.2.10,cust2,mtu 1500), c3-host(172.16.3.10,cust3,mtu 1500), ext-dns1(8.8.8.10,internet,mtu 1500), ext-dns2(1.1.1.10,internet,mtu 1500), noc1(10.99.0.10,noc,mtu 1500), noc2(10.99.0.11,noc,mtu 1500), noclab1(10.98.0.10,noc-lab,mtu 1500), noclab2(10.98.0.11,noc-lab,mtu 1500)
Routers: SEA, PAO, SDG, SLC, BOU, HOU, LNK, CHM, PIT, ATL, AAR, ITH, PRN, CPK, cust1, cust2, cust3, peer1, peer2
text:
The diff does the opposite of the ticket's intent on PRN: PRN's deny entry matches 172.16.0.0/16 le 24, which covers all customer prefixes (172.16.1.0/24, 172.16.2.0/24, 172.16.3.0/24). PRN would stop redistributing every customer route into OSPF. CPK correctly stops injecting only customer 3. The tests below check that customer 3's route is still injected via PRN and that customers 1 and 2 are unaffected, which will expose the PRN problem.
